questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2.
questions.solution:
The correct option to fill in the blank No. 2 is "seemed" as it makes the sentence grammatically and contextually correct.

 Key Points

  • Seemed: This is the past tense of the verb "seem," which is used to indicate an apparent state or condition, or to make something appear in a certain way. For instance, "She seemed happy," suggests that she appeared to be happy, but it doesn't necessarily mean that she was truly happy.

Additional Information

  • Perhaps: This is an adverb that indicates uncertainty or possibility. It is used when you are not certain about something. For example, in the sentence, "Perhaps it will rain later," the speaker is suggesting that it might rain later, but they aren't sure.
  • Besides: This can function as a preposition or an adverb. As a preposition, it means 'in addition to' or 'apart from'. For example, "Besides basketball, she also plays tennis," meaning she plays tennis in addition to basketball. As an adverb, it can mean 'moreover' or 'also'. For example, "I don't want to go to the party. Besides, I have to study," where 'besides' introduces an additional reason.
  • Thought: This is the past tense of the verb "think," which means to have a particular belief or idea. It also refers to the act or process of considering, believing, or remembering something. For example, "I thought you were going to the store," suggests that the speaker previously believed that the other person was going to the store.

  • Seemed: "Seemed" का अर्थ होता है "प्रतीत होना". यह शब्द एक स्थिति या अवस्था को दिखाने या किसी चीज़ को एक निश्चित तरह से प्रदर्शित करने के लिए इस्तेमाल किया जाता है।
  • उदाहरण के लिए, "वह खुश प्रतीत हुई," का अर्थ होता है कि वह खुश दिख रही थी, लेकिन यह अवश्य नहीं है कि वह वास्तव में खुश थी।
  • Perhaps: "Perhaps" का मतलब होता है "शायद" या "संभव". यह तब इस्तेमाल किया जाता है जब आप किसी चीज़ के प्रति निश्चित नहीं होते।
  • उदाहरण के लिए, "शायद बाद में बारिश हो सकती है," का मतलब होता है कि शायद बाद में बारिश हो सकती है, लेकिन वक्ता सुनिश्चित नहीं है।
  • Besides: "Besides" का अर्थ होता है "के अलावा" या "साथ ही". यह एक पूर्वसर्ग या क्रिया-विशेषण के रूप में कार्य कर सकता है।

  • Thought: "Thought" का अर्थ होता है "सोचा". यह "सोचना" के क्रिया का भूतकाल है, जो किसी विशेष विचार या आस्था को दर्शता है। यह किसी चीज़ को विचार करने, विश्वास करने, या याद करने की प्रक्रिया को भी दर्शाता है।
  • उदाहरण के लिए, "मैंने सोचा कि आप दुकान जा रहे थे," का अर्थ होता है कि वक्ता ने पहले सोचा था कि दूसरा व्यक्ति दुकान जा रहा था।

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer to fill in the blank number 2 is option 1, "next."

Key Points

  • The word next means coming immediately after the present one in order, rank, or space.

  • "In the very next" is a phrase used to describe something that is happening immediately following the current event or situation. This phrase is often used in temporal and sequential contexts.

  • Here are a few examples:

    • "In the very next chapter of the book, the mystery of the haunted house is revealed."

      • This means that the mystery will be revealed immediately in the following chapter.

    • "In the very next game, the team made a fantastic comeback."

      • This implies that the team had a great performance in the game immediately after the current one.

  • In the context of the passage, the word next indicates that the very next entry in the diary shows a major gap in time and events from the previous one. 
  • Hence, "next," is the most appropriate choice for filling in the blank number 2 in this sentence.

Additional Information

  • Option 2, "former," would not make sense in this context as it refers to something that was previously in a certain state or position. For example, "My former boss was very strict."
  • Option 3, "earlier," could work in this sentence, but it would change the meaning slightly. It would imply that the meeting was originally scheduled for a later date but has been moved up.  For example, "I was supposed to meet with my boss next week, but we moved it to an earlier date."
  • Option 4, "over," would not make sense in this context as it means to be finished or concluded. For example, "The meeting is over, and we can all go home now."
  •  Next (अगला) - Coming immediately after the time or order in consideration.
    • Example: The next meeting is scheduled for Monday.
  • Former (पूर्व) - Occurring in the past or before the present time; previous.
    • Example: The former president visited his old school.
  • Earlier (पहले) - Happening or done before a particular time.
    • Example: If only she had known about it earlier.
  • Over (समाप्त) - Finished; concluded.
    • Example: The match was over within a couple of hours.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'are'.
 
Key Points
  • The subject "Dolphins" is plural, so the correct auxiliary verb is "are."
  • The sentence is written in present tense, describing a general truth about dolphins.
  • 'Are regarded' is the correct passive construction showing dolphins are considered friendly by people.
  • Options like "is," "was," or "has" do not agree with the plural subject or tense requirement.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 3'.
 
Complete Passage: Dolphins 1. are regarded as the friendliest creatures in the sea, and stories of them helping drowning sailors have been common since Roman times. The more we 2. ____about dolphins, the more we realise that their society is more complex 3. ____people previously imagined. They look 4. ____other dolphins when they are ill, care for pregnant 5. ____and protect the weakest in the community, as we do.
 
Additional Information
  • Has: Incorrect, as "has regarded" is grammatically wrong here and mismatched with plural subject.
  • Was: Incorrect, as it indicates past tense, while the passage describes a present truth.
  • Is: Incorrect, as "is" is singular and does not agree with plural "dolphins."
